blockers.message: the review record has no `## code.review` section, while roles were active at it
R-ops-1 (The switch to Paylane has no way back once Stripe is closed) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it
R-ops-2 (Nobody would see the settlement worker fail or not run) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.evidence:
The Stripe client is deleted and replaced by the Paylane client in the same
release. There is no switch between the two: keeping both would double the
code to maintain. The Stripe account is closed the day after the release.
findings.location: design.md#Decision: All traffic moves at deploy
findings.recommendation: Keep a way back for the provider switch-over. If Paylane fails in production (outage, authorizations rejected, a bad integration found after the release), the only recourse is redeploying the previous version — and once the Stripe account is closed the day after, that version can no longer take a single card payment: checkout is down with no rollback, and a weekly release cadence makes a forward fix slow. Keep the Stripe client behind a configuration switch (or a feature flag) for at least one release cycle, keep the Stripe account open until Paylane has run in production without incident for an agreed period, and add the switch and the account closure as explicit tasks with a rollback procedure.
findings.title: The switch to Paylane has no way back once Stripe is closed

findings.evidence:
A new worker, `settlement-worker`, runs at 02:00, fetches the day's Paylane
payments and matches them to orders. It runs as a Kubernetes CronJob and
writes its result to the database.
findings.location: design.md#Decision: A worker settles payments nightly
findings.recommendation: Make the new CronJob observable. The design's only signal is the finance alert for an unmatched payment (spec "A payment without order"); if the job fails (Paylane API down, database error, crash) or never starts (CronJob suspended, schedule missed), no row is written and no alert fires, so the day's payments go unreconciled and an operator sees nothing. Decide in the design how a failed or missed run is detected — a structured log at start and end with the counts processed, a success metric or last-success timestamp with an alert when it is older than a day, and an alert on job failure — and add it to task 1.2.
findings.title: Nobody would see the settlement worker fail or not run
